extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers learning category theory (advanced undergraduates / graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, equivalent formulations, and key properties of adjunctions (units, counits, triangular identities), plus related notions (reflective subcategories, equivalence of categories, Galois connections) used to construct or verify adjoints in categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction via natural bijection (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjunction (F, G, φ): X ~ A is given by functors F: X -> A, G: A -> X and a family of bijections φ: A(Fx,a) ≅ X(x,Ga), natural in x and a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bijection φ is required to be natural in both variables; this bijection is the fundamental datum from which unit and counit arise (φ and φ^{-1} appear in formulas (6) and (7) in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit η and universal property of η_x
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit η : 1_X -> G F is a natural transformation such that for each object x the arrow η_x : x -> G F x is universal to G from x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universality means: for each f: x -> G a there is exactly one g: F x -> a with G g ∘ η_x = f; this induces the bijection φ(A(Fx,a)) → X(x,Ga) via φ(f) = G f ∘ η_x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counit ε and universal property of ε_a
rubrics_metrics.description: The counit ε : F G -> 1_A is a natural transformation such that for each object a the arrow ε_a : F G a -> a is universal from F to a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universality means: for each g: x -> G a there is exactly one f: F x -> a with ε_a ∘ F g = f; φ^{-1} is given by φ^{-1}(g) = ε_a ∘ F g (formula (7) in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangular identities (unit-counit composites are identities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two composites G ε ∘ η G and ε F ∘ F η are the identity natural transformations of G and F respectively (written in text as G~GFG~G and F~FGF~F or equations (8)/(9)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'triangular identities' are equivalent to the adjunction and are often used as the defining relations in place of the bijection φ; they do not make explicit use of objects and are convenient for manipulation. They also make η a 'quasi-inverse' to ε in some authors' language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent data describing an adjunction (Theorem 2, item (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Functors F, G and a natural transformation η: 1_X -> G F such that each η_x is universal to G from x determine an adjunction (with φ defined by (6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formulation says an adjunction can be specified by unit + universality of its components; given η with universality properties one recovers φ and the whole adjunction uniquely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent data describing an adjunction (Theorem 2, item (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor G: A -> X and for each x ∈ X an object F x ∈ A with a universal arrow η_x: x -> G F x determine a left adjoint F (object function F0) and the natural η.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The functor F is defined on arrows h: x -> x' by the unique arrow F h making the universality diagrams commute (G F h ∘ η_x = η_{x'} ∘ h). This is the 'construct adjoint from universal arrows' recipe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent data describing an adjunction (Theorem 2, item (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Functors F, G and a natural transformation ε: F G -> 1_A such that each ε_a is universal from F to a determine an adjunction (with φ^{-1} defined by (7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the dual of (i): specifying counit with universality of its components uniquely determines the adjunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent data describing an adjunction (Theorem 2, item (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor F: X -> A and for each a ∈ A an object G a ∈ X with an arrow ε_a: F G a -> a universal from F to a determine a right adjoint G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual to (ii): given universal arrows from F to each a, one constructs the right adjoint G and counit components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent data describing an adjunction (Theorem 2, item (v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Functors F, G and natural transformations η: 1_X -> G F and ε: F G -> 1_A such that both composites (G ε) ∘ (η G) and (ε F) ∘ (F η) are identity determine an adjunction (and φ defined from η or ε).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formulation packages the adjunction as unit+counit satisfying the triangular identities; from these one recovers the bijection φ and hence the adjunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of adjoints up to natural isomorphism (Corollary 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any two left-adjoints F and F' of a fixed functor G: A -> X are naturally isomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses uniqueness of universal arrows: for each x both η_x: x -> G F x and η'_x: x -> G F' x are universal, so there is a unique isomorphism θ_x: F x -> F' x with G θ_x ∘ η_x = η'_x; these θ_x assemble into a natural iso θ: F ≅ F'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability criterion for existence of left adjoint (Corollary 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor G: A -> X has a left adjoint if and only if for each x ∈ X the functor X(x, G -) : A -> Set is representable (i.e., isomorphic to A(Fx, -) for some Fx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If φ: A(Fx,a) ≅ X(x,Ga) is such a representation natural in a, then the object-function Fx is the object function of a left adjoint of G and gives the adjunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoints of additive functors are additive (Theorem 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G: A -> M is an additive functor between Ab-categories and G has a left adjoint F, then F is additive and the adjunction bijections φ: A(F m, a) ≅ M(m, G a) are isomorphisms of abelian groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: naturality and additivity of G and properties of the unit η imply φ(f+f') = φ(f) + φ(f'), and universality shows F preserves addition on arrows; dually, right adjoints of additive functors are additive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits/colimits as instances of adjoints (universal arrow criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a universal arrow from (or to) every object (e.g., from diagonal functor to each pair (a,b)) constructs adjoints that produce limits/colimits: e.g., products as right adjoint to diagonal, coproducts as left adjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely, product a × b is the object representing C(c,a) × C(c,b) ≅ C(c,a×b); the counit gives projections and φ sends f:c->a×b to the pair (p f, q f). Existence of universal arrows is an 'easy' way to show adjoints/limits exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective subcategory characterization and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A full subcategory A ⊆ B is reflective when the inclusion K: A -> B has a left adjoint F: B -> A (the reflector); equivalently there is R = K F: B -> B with values in A and a natural bijection A(R b, a) ≅ B(b, a) natural in b ∈ B and a ∈ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: to each b ∈ B there is R b ∈ A and arrow ρ_b: b -> R b universal among arrows from b to objects of A. For reflections (inclusions are faithful) counit components are epi; more generally, if G is faithful then every counit ε_a is epi; G full iff every ε_a is split monic; full+faithful iff each ε_a is iso (Theorem 1 in reflective section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of categories: three equivalent characterizations (Theorem 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a functor S: A -> C the following are equivalent: (i) S is an equivalence of categories; (ii) S is part of an adjoint equivalence (T, S; η, ε) with unit and counit isomorphisms; (iii) S is full and faithful and each object c ∈ C is isomorphic to S a for some a ∈ A (essentially surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: from (iii) one constructs a left adjoint T by choosing for each c an a with an iso c ≅ S a; the resulting unit and counit are isomorphisms and give an adjoint equivalence. Adjoint equivalence implies both unit and counit are natural isomorphisms and satisfy triangular identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint equivalence / adjoint-left-inverse notion
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjoint equivalence is an adjunction (T, S; η, ε) in which both η and ε are natural isomorphisms; then T is both a left and right adjoint of S and inverse up to iso. A left-adjoint-left-inverse is an adjunction (F,G;η,1) whose counit is the identity; then G is an isomorphism onto a reflective subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangular identities simplify when unit/counit are isomorphisms; in particular, if the subcategory is full and every object of the larger category is iso to an object of the subcategory then the inclusion is part of an adjoint equivalence with identity counit (Proposition 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois connections as adjoint pairs for preorders
rubrics_metrics.description: For preorders P and Q and order-preserving L: P -> Q^{op}, R: Q^{op} -> P, L (as a functor) is left adjoint to R iff for all p ∈ P and q ∈ Q, L p ≤ q in Q iff p ≤ R q in P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because hom-sets have at most one arrow in preorders, the bijection condition reduces to this equivalence of inequalities; unit and counit become the inequalities p ≤ R L p and L R q ≤ q (triangular identities). This is the standard notion of Galois connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct and inverse image adjoints (examples: quantifiers as adjoints)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a map f: U -> V, the inverse image f^*: P(V) -> P(U) has both a left adjoint (direct image with existential quantifier ∃_f) and a right adjoint (universal image ∀_f), satisfying X ⊆ f^*(Y) iff f_!(X) ⊆ Y and f^*(S) ⊆ X iff S ⊆ f_*(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This example interprets logical connectives and quantifiers as adjoints: union/intersection as adjoints to diagonal; projection inverse image has left and right adjoints corresponding to ∃ and ∀. It illustrates how to look for adjoints in set-theoretic constructions.
